claims: Administer intravenous fluids to maintain hydration and renal perfusion.
Monitor electrolyte levels, particularly potassium, due to elevated levels and ongoing diuretic use.
Elevate the head of the bed to reduce the risk of aspiration in the setting of altered mental status.
Initiate mechanical ventilation if oxygen saturation remains <92% despite supplemental oxygen.
Administer intravenous heparin to prevent thromboembolic events given prolonged prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time.
Monitor coagulation profile closely, including PT, PTT, and INR.
Initiate physical therapy to prevent muscle atrophy and improve mobility, if the patient’s condition allows.
Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics to treat suspected sepsis, given the elevated troponin levels and renal dysfunction.
Administer medications for pain management, given the moderate to severe pain reported.
Administer oral or intravenous thyroid hormone replacement if the patient is hypothyroid, based on the low thyroid stimulating hormone and normal thyroxine levels.
